title: Reddit tests AI shopping feature Reviews, which can automatically summarize product reviews and purchase links

content_html:
Reddit has announced that it is testing an AI shopping feature called “Reviews.” It uses artificial intelligence to aggregate product discussions among users on the platform, generating product summaries, purchase links, and pros and cons analyses to help users understand authentic product reviews and support purchasing decisions. The feature will consolidate community discussions across categories such as skincare, coffee, and headphones, display product reviews in search results, and highlight product mentions in post comment sections.

This test covers areas including electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel, involving about 10,000 products. Reddit had previously launched a small-scale pilot in February 2026, initially focused mainly on electronics. If the test performs well, the company plans to further expand product categories and extend the service to markets outside the United States.

However, the new feature has sparked opposition from some moderators and users. They worry that even if product links are not paid ads, they could still disrupt community discussions and increase stealth marketing and commercial spam, especially when some subreddits have no opt-out mechanism. Reddit responded that Reviews is generated entirely based on internal platform content, does not scrape or repost third-party information, and product links are not paid ad slots; users can follow the links back to the original discussions to view the context.

The feature also faces challenges related to the authenticity of AI content. Because Reddit relies on user discussions and anonymous community mechanisms, marketers, organized deceptive promotion, and AI-generated spam comments could all affect the credibility of the summaries. Reddit says it is strengthening spam detection and bot governance.

This test reflects the platform’s attempt to turn community content into an entry point for shopping decisions, but how to strike a balance between commercialization and community trust remains a problem it needs to solve.
